# pidginhost_dns_zone (Resource)

FreeDNS hosting for a domain: the zone pidginhost_dns_record adds records to. Activating the zone of an internal domain points the domain's name servers at PidginHost. Destroying the resource deactivates FreeDNS: the zone is deleted with all its records and an internal domain gets back the name servers it had before. Destroying an already inactive zone also succeeds. Do not manage the name servers of the same domain with pidginhost_domain_nameservers.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "pidginhost_dns_zone" "example" {
  domain = "example.com"
  ip     = "192.0.2.10"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `domain` (String) Domain name, such as example.com. Changing it replaces the zone.
- `ip` (String) IPv4 address of the A record the API adds for the domain when it activates the zone. It is only used then: changing it later changes nothing in the zone. To manage that A record with pidginhost_dns_record, import it.

### Optional

- `source` (String) internal for a domain registered with PidginHost, external for a domain added to the account in the PidginHost panel. Defaults to internal. Changing it replaces the resource.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) <domain>/<source>.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a zone by "<domain>/<source>", where source is internal or external.
terraform import pidginhost_dns_zone.example example.com/internal
```
